evals.prompt: I've finished building my plugin 'git-summary' — it's in ~/projects/git-summary-plugin. It has skills, hooks for all four runtimes, and I want to publish it to the universal plugin marketplace. Walk me through the full publish process.
evals.expected_output: Runs pre-flight validation checks on all four vendor manifests and plugin.json metadata, then prepares the registry entry JSON and guides opening a PR to the registry repo. Should check hook casing per vendor.

evals.prompt: I'm trying to submit my 'code-formatter' plugin to the marketplace but I think there might be validation errors. The plugin is at /tmp/code-formatter. Can you check if it's ready and fix any issues before submitting?
evals.expected_output: Runs pre-flight checks, identifies specific validation failures (e.g., missing Codex manifest, wrong hook casing on Cursor manifest, missing license field), reports them clearly, and asks user to fix before proceeding to Step 2.

evals.prompt: My plugin 'ai-commit' is listed in the universal marketplace at version 1.0.0. I've just released v1.1.0 (tag ai-commit@1.1.0) with some new hooks. Publish the new version.
evals.expected_output: Treats this as the normal publish flow, not a separate update request. Reads 1.1.0 from plugin.json, confirms tag ai-commit@1.1.0 exists on the remote and records its commit, finds the entry listed at 1.0.0 in each catalog, and moves it in place with `marketplace update` (--ref ai-commit@1.1.0, --sha <commit> when the entry pins a sha, --version 1.1.0 when it carries one, plus any changed description) rather than adding a second entry. Keeps curator fields and the original publishedAt, adds updatedAt, and opens one PR covering every catalog the marketplace carries.

evals.prompt: My plugin 'foo' lives at packages/foo/plugin.json inside a monorepo (the repo root only has a marketplace.json catalog, no plugin.json). Publish it to cyberuni/cyberplace.
evals.expected_output: Determines the plugin is not at the repo root and has no npm packagePath, so decides source type git-subdir rather than a root-clone url. Writes { "source": "git-subdir", "url": "<clone-url>.git", "path": "packages/foo" } in the marketplace entry. Runs marketplace validate against the marketplace working copy before opening the PR, and does not proceed if it fails.

evals.prompt: I'm a maintainer of cyberuni/cyberplace and I already have it checked out here. I want to add a plugin called 'db-migrate' that lives at github.com/someuser/db-migrate. Add it.
evals.expected_output: Detects the cwd is the marketplace repo itself, not the plugin, so it reads the plugin's metadata from the given URL (cloning it to a scratch location) instead of the cwd, then works directly in the existing checkout (fetch/merge, branch, edit, commit, push, PR) rather than cloning or forking cyberuni/cyberplace again. The prepared entry's source/repository URL points at db-migrate's repo, not at cyberuni/cyberplace.

evals.prompt: Publish buddy-agent-harness (in ~/code/buddy-agent-harness) to the cyberplace marketplace. Its plugin.json declares dependencies ["agent-harness", { "name": "cyber-asana", "marketplace": "cyberuni" }]. cyberplace's .claude-plugin/marketplace.json does not list agent-harness and has no allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn.
evals.expected_output: Reads the plugin's dependencies before submitting. Treats "agent-harness" as a plain dependency resolved against cyberplace: since cyberplace does not list it, prepares agent-harness's entry in the same PR from its own repository/package (after pre-flight), or stops and tells the user to publish agent-harness first — never opens a PR listing buddy-agent-harness without it. Treats cyber-asana@cyberuni as a named-marketplace dependency: adds no entry for it, says installs from cyberplace need "cyberuni" in allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn, and offers to add it.

evals.prompt: Publish cyber-asana (in ~/code/cyber-asana, a monorepo with the plugin at packages/cyber-asana, released as tag cyber-asana@1.2.0) to anthropics/claude-plugins-official. Its plugin.json declares the plain dependency "cyber-agentkit".
evals.expected_output: Before preparing a PR, runs `gh repo view anthropics/claude-plugins-official --json viewerPermission`, sees READ, then reads the target's .github/workflows/ for a workflow that closes outside PRs and its README's Contributing section. Concludes the catalog is curated (outside PRs are closed automatically; new plugins go through a submission form), so it does not clone, fork, branch, push, or open a PR. Runs pre-flight, resolves cyber-agentkit against the target's live catalog and tells the user it will not resolve there, and drafts the entry in the shape the catalog's existing entries use (e.g. a git-subdir source pinned with the release tag as ref and that tag's commit as sha). Hands the user the draft and the submission form link the target names. Does not rely on remembered facts about that catalog.

evals.prompt: Publish my plugin 'git-summary' (cwd is its repo). Its .agents/universal-plugin.json has no marketplaces key.
evals.expected_output: Runs `config get --key marketplaces --format json --root <plugin-root>`, gets [], and with no target named in the request resolves the target to the fallback cyber-uni/marketplace. Tells the user the target is cyber-uni/marketplace and that it came from the fallback default before any PR step. Does not target cyberuni/cyberplace.

evals.prompt: Publish my plugin 'git-summary' (cwd is its repo). Its .agents/universal-plugin.json has "marketplaces": [{"name":"cyber-uni","repo":"cyber-uni/marketplace"},{"name":"team","repo":"acme/plugins"}].
evals.expected_output: Reads the marketplaces key through `config get --key marketplaces`, reports both targets as coming from .agents/universal-plugin.json, and publishes to each one with its own PR (Steps 0b to 3 once per target). Does not fall back to cyber-uni/marketplace as an extra target, and does not merge both into one PR.

evals.prompt: Publish my plugin 'git-summary' to team. Its .agents/universal-plugin.json has "marketplaces": [{"name":"cyber-uni","repo":"cyber-uni/marketplace"},{"name":"team","repo":"acme/plugins"}].
evals.expected_output: Resolves the named entry 'team' to acme/plugins, reports it as named in the request, and opens one PR against acme/plugins only, not against cyber-uni/marketplace.

evals.prompt: Publish my plugin 'ai-commit' (plugin.json says 1.1.0) to cyber-uni/marketplace.
evals.expected_output: Resolves tag ai-commit@1.1.0, then finds every cyber-uni/marketplace catalog already lists ai-commit at 1.1.0 pinned to that tag. Reports that 1.1.0 is already published there, naming the catalogs, and changes nothing: no branch, no commit, no PR.

evals.prompt: I bumped 'ai-commit' to 1.2.0 in plugin.json. Release it to the marketplace.
evals.expected_output: Checks the remote for the release tag (ai-commit@1.2.0 or v1.2.0) with git ls-remote, finds none, and stops before touching any catalog: says the tag is missing and the version must be released and the tag pushed first. Does not pin the default branch or a nonexistent ref, and opens no PR.

evals.prompt: Publish 'git-summary' v0.1.0 (tag git-summary@0.1.0 exists) to cyber-uni/marketplace. It has never been listed there.
evals.expected_output: Resolves the tag, finds no catalog lists git-summary, and adds the entry to every catalog the marketplace carries in one PR titled 'Add git-summary v0.1.0', pinning the release where the catalog's entries pin refs.

evals.prompt: Publish clibuilder 12.4.0 to cyber-uni/marketplace. The plugin lives at packages/clibuilder in clibuilder/clibuilder; that folder's package.json is public and its files list plugin.json, skills/ and the vendor manifests. .agents/universal-plugin.json declares no packagePath.
evals.expected_output: Runs config get --key packagePath --infer, reads ".", and confirms the tarball carries plugin.json (npm view / npm pack --dry-run). Lists Claude Code and Codex with { "source": "npm", "package": "clibuilder" }, lists Copilot CLI and Cursor from git (git-subdir at packages/clibuilder pinned to the release tag) rather than leaving them out, and tells the user to declare "packagePath": "." in the plugin's .agents/universal-plugin.json.
